summary: A cardholder makes a small purchase early in the billing cycle, receives a statement, and pays the full statement balance before the listed due date. The scenario tests that the account stays within the credit limit, the minimum-payment obligation is satisfied on time, and the issuer provides the purchase grace period so no late fee or over-limit fee is triggered.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of this billing cycle, so the purchase qualifies for the grace-period condition in clause.6.grace_period.
The issuer has approved a credit limit of $1000.00, and the single purchase in this scenario does not exceed that limit.

The statement for this cycle closes on 2025-05-31 and shows a New Balance of $200.00, making the minimum payment $15.00 under the contract formula; paying $200.00 satisfies clause.5.minimum_payment_obligation in full.
The payment is made through an approved standard payment method and is credited on the date received, with no returned payment.
No cash advance, international transaction, disputed charge, skipped payment, or default event occurs in this scenario.
Because the payment is made in full on or before the due date, the archetype expects no late payment fee and no over-limit fee.
